title: STF's VitorIA identifies at least 247 similar appeals in the controversy behind Tema 1.261; Plenary finds no general repercussion on 22 August 2023
summary: VitorIA identified at least 247 similar appeals in the controversy behind Tema 1.261; STF Plenary found no general repercussion on 22 August 2023 (final 23 September 2023)
account: Brazil's Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) uses VitorIA, operational since 2023, to compare the texts of incoming appeals and group cases raising similar legal questions for the staff who screen candidates for repercussão geral themes; the court states the tool does not judge cases. On 28 September 2026 the STF said that in the controversy that gave rise to Tema 1.261 (leading case ARE 1441934, on municipal teachers' personal pay advantages) VitorIA identified at least 247 appeals with similar legal questions by grouping on content similarity, adding that finding so many similar cases did not determine the result. The theme record shows the Plenary decided unanimously on 22 August 2023 that there is no general repercussion because the question is infraconstitutional, final on 23 September 2023; no cited source states what then happened to the 247 appeals. The STF credits VitorIA with four themes in 2023, 19 in 2024 and 11 in 2025, and says these figures do not refer to decisions taken with AI help and do not allow calculating accuracy or time saved.
purpose: Identify clusters of textually similar appeals so the court can treat them jointly or open new general-repercussion themes
system: VitorIA (STF), textual-similarity clustering tool that groups appeals raising similar legal questions; in development in 2022 and operational in 2023 per the STF
developer: Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF); the STF's 28 Sep 2026 item names no external developer and does not link VitorIA to the court's earlier Victor project

ratings.reason: No individual beneficiary or per-party outcome is documented; the STF says its figures do not refer to decisions taken with AI help and do not allow calculating time saved.

Material to the court's screening work: in one controversy VitorIA identified at least 247 appeals with similar legal questions, which the STF describes as the technology taking part in organizing and identifying patterns in its case flow; the STF does not quantify time saved.
Small at system scale; one theme among the 34 the STF credits to VitorIA for 2023–2025.

ai_role.statement: The STF states the tool's function is prior to judgment: “identificar grupos de casos parecidos, que depois passam pela análise das equipes responsáveis e, quando necessário, dos ministros.” The identification of at least 247 similar appeals is attributed to VitorIA by the court itself, which adds that finding them “não determinou o resultado”; the theme decision was made by the Plenary. Developer and deployer are the same public body (STF): the STF news items are the court documenting its own tool, and no cited source names an external developer or links VitorIA to the court's earlier Victor project (STF with UnB), whose classifier the STF said in August 2021 was not yet in production.
